exclude_keywords <- c( "edible",  "food", "biofuel", "continue", "still",
                       "\\?", "station", "gasoline", "diesel")

# Filter out rows where 'title' contains any of the exclude keywords

Graphique pour regarder les news

```{r}
full_dates <- tibble(datetime = seq(min(news_data_vdif$datetime, na.rm=TRUE), max(news_data_vdif$datetime, na.rm=TRUE), by = "day"))

# Fusionner le DataFrame original avec la séquence complète de dates
complete_data <- full_dates %>%
  left_join(full_news_count , by = "datetime") %>%
  replace_na(list(news_per_day = 0))


ggplot(complete_data, aes(x = datetime, y = news_per_day)) +
  geom_line() +
  labs(title = "Number of news per day",
       x = "Date",
       y = "Number of news") +
  theme_minimal()
```


```{r}

cluster_labels <- c(
  "Global Gas Trade and Regional Cooperation", 
  "Major Gas Supply Agreements", 
  "Supply Chain and Infrastructure Challenges in Oil & Gas", 
  "European Gas Crisis and Russia’s Role", 
  "Geopolitics of Gas in the Middle East and Asia", 
  "Gas Pipeline Disruptions and Cybersecurity", 
  "New Pipeline Projects and Developments", 
  "Energy Crisis and Gas Price Volatility", 
  "Natural Gas Market Trends and Demand Forecasts", 
  "Pipeline Projects in Developing Regions", 
  "Supply Chain and Emergency Response", 
  "Infrastructure Expansion and Gas Production"
)
# Créer un dataframe avec les types d'événements
event_types <- data.frame(cluster_label = cluster_labels)

# Créer toutes les combinaisons de dates et d'événements
full_event_dates <- full_dates %>%
  crossing(event_types)

# Joindre avec les données de nouvelles
event_complete_data <- full_event_dates %>%
  left_join(cluster_news_count, by = c("datetime", "cluster_label")) %>%
  replace_na(list(news_per_day = 0))

ggplot(event_complete_data, aes(x = datetime, y = news_per_day, color = cluster_label)) +
  geom_line() +
  labs(title = "Number of news per day",
       x = "Date",
       y = "Number of news") +
  theme_minimal()
```


```{r}
ggplot(event_complete_data, aes(x = datetime, y = news_per_day, color = cluster_label)) +
  geom_line(legend=FALSE) +
  labs(title = "Number of news per day",
       x = "Date",
       y = "Number of news")  +
  theme(legend.position = "none") 
```



# With BERT embeddings

On fait exctement la même chose mais avec un autre algorithme pour établir les embeddings


```{r}
setwd('C:/Users/DBT3KD/Desktop/Etude_macro_elec/prix_electricite_gitlab/gas_code')
# Import the functions from 'my_functions.R'
Sys.setenv(lang = "en_US")

news_data_bert <- read.csv("clustered_articles_bert_labeled_full_sample.csv")

news_data_bert
```


```{r}
Sys.setlocale("LC_TIME", "English")

news_data_bert$datetime <- as.Date(format(as.Date(news_data_bert$date, "%b %d, %Y"), "%Y-%m-%d"))

Sys.setlocale("LC_TIME", "C")

get_date <- function(original_date){
  # Remplacer "Sept" par "Sep" pour que R le reconnaisse
  corrected_date <- gsub("Sept", "Sep", original_date)
  
  # Convert to Date object in the desired format
  formatted_date <- as.Date(corrected_date, format = "%d %b %Y")
  datetime <- as.Date(format(formatted_date, "%Y-%m-%d"))
  return(datetime)
}

news_data_bert$datetime <- ifelse( is.na(news_data_bert$datetime),
                                   get_date(news_data_bert$date),
                                   news_data_bert$datetime)


news_data_bert <- news_data_bert %>% 
  mutate(datetime = as.Date(datetime)) %>% 
  arrange(datetime)

full_news_count <- news_data_bert %>% 
  select(media, datetime) %>%
  distinct() %>% 
  group_by(datetime) %>% 
  summarise(news_per_day = n())

cluster_news_count <- news_data_bert %>% 
  select(media, datetime, cluster, cluster_label) %>%
  distinct() %>% 
  group_by(datetime, cluster, cluster_label) %>% 
  summarise(news_per_day = n())
```


```{r}

cluster_labels <- unique(news_data_bert$cluster_label)

# Créer un dataframe avec les types d'événements
cluster_types <- data.frame(cluster_label = cluster_labels)

full_dates <- tibble(datetime = seq(min(news_data_bert$datetime, na.rm=TRUE), max(news_data_bert$datetime, na.rm=TRUE), by = "day"))
# Créer toutes les combinaisons de dates et d'événements
full_cluster_dates <- full_dates %>%
  crossing(cluster_types)

# Joindre avec les données de nouvelles
cluster_complete_data <- full_cluster_dates %>%
  left_join(cluster_news_count, by = c("datetime", "cluster_label")) %>%
  replace_na(list(news_per_day = 0))

ggplot(cluster_complete_data, aes(x = datetime, y = news_per_day, color = cluster_label)) +
  geom_line() +
  labs(title = "Number of news per day",
       x = "Date",
       y = "Number of news") +
  theme_minimal()
```

```{r}
shock_data <- cluster_complete_data %>%
  arrange(datetime) %>%  # Replace 'date_column' with your actual date column name
  mutate(moving_avg_news = rollapply(news_per_day, width = 30, FUN = mean, fill = NA, align = "right"),
        moving_std_news = rollapply(news_per_day, width = 30, FUN = sd, fill = NA, align = "right"),
       binary_shock= (news_per_day >  moving_avg_news + 1.96*moving_std_news),
       intensity_shock = ifelse(binary_shock, news_per_day/moving_avg_news, 0)
       )

instrument_days <- shock_data %>% 
  filter(binary_shock == TRUE & news_per_day>=3)
instrument_days
```
